KEY MESSAGE 1: Minimal pre-Thanksgiving travel weather impacts 

Strong high pressure overhead will keep Pennsylvania dry the
rest of today. This high pressure will pivot off to the east 
tonight as a surface trough develops over the Ohio Valley and 
Western Pennsylvania. Coupled with a deepening surface low off 
the coast of Florida, the resulting pressure gradient will allow
for gusty winds over the Laurel Highlands today with gusts 
between 20 and 25 mph. These winds will increase in strength 
into the overnight ahead of the Thanksgiving day coastal storm. 

KEY MESSAGE 2: Damaging winds and widespread rain for
Thanksgiving Day 

Widespread soaking of 1 to 2 inches of rainfall expected on 
Thanksgiving Day as a very strong easterly low level flow 
associated with a powerful coastal storm system transports 
anomalous moisture into central PA. Latest model guidance hints
at an arrival for precipitation to cross the MD boarder a 
around 7AM. This rain will spread northwards throughout the 
morning and afternoon across the whole state. The heaviest rain 
is currently projected to fall between 7AM Thu and 1AM Fri.
Strong upper level frontogenesis and warm air advection ahead of
the low pressure system's center may allow for some locally
heavier precipitation bands to move through the state. Elevated
instability working up Thursday afternoon into the evening may 
also yield a rumble of thunder or two. 

Strong to damaging wind gusts are expected with this system, 
particularly over the southeastern third of the CWA and the
Laurel Highlands. Recent runs of some of the deterministic 
models, including the GFS and ECMWF continue to show a 60 to 90
knot 850 mb low- level easterly jet developing in response to 
the strong pressure gradient between the deepening low to the 
south and retreating high pressure to the north. It remains to 
be seen how much of this wind will be able to make it down to 
the surface, but soundings from the GFS show 45-50 knot winds at
the top of the mixed layer Thursday afternoon over the Lower 
Susquehanna Valley. The REFS ensemble supports this with, 50+ 
kt winds being able to make it down to the surface with the area
of interest being the the Lower Susquehanna Valley as well in 
the ensemble mean. 

With all of this in mind, a High Wind Warning remains in place for
Lancaster, Lebanon, and Schuylkill counties. The Laurel 
Highlands are expected to see gusts up to 50-55 mph Thursday 
through Saturday, and there remains some thinking that a High 
Wind Warning may be needed for the strongest downslope winds on 
Thursday over the Laurels, but we have opted for issuing a Wind 
Advisory for now. Areas downwind of terrain features will be
places to watch for isolated 60+ mph gusts such as the Laural
Highlands but also eastern Franklin County and southern Sullivan
County. Elsewhere in PA gusts of 40 to 45 mph are possible and 
a Wind Advisory remaining in place for most of our counties 
where confidence in these gusts are highest. Timing of strongest
winds will be Thursday afternoon. With such a strong warm air
advection regime in place, we opted to increase low temperatures
Thursday night given the cloud cover, so less diurnal 
temperature variability will be in place into Friday. 

Of note, the strong winds on Thursday will be from the east 
which anecdotally does tend to cause more tree damage since 
trees are "tested" a lot less frequently from the east than from
the north or west in this region. All and all, the wind and 
rain will make for hazardous travel conditions. Unfortunately, 
isolated to scattered power outages will be possible on

KEY MESSAGE 3: Breezy on Friday with rain showers/elevation snow 

Colder air will gradually wrap back into Pennsylvania late 
Thursday night and Friday as the system stacks up along the
North-Central Appalachians. This should allow for snow to begin
mixing in especially over the higher terrain from the Laurel
Highlands northward along the Allegheny Plateau into northern
PA. Rain/snow mix during the day Friday beneath the stacked low
transitions to more of a lake effect/upslope precip pattern 
Friday night into Saturday as the system lifts into New England.
As a back-end 805mb jet works its way into southwest PA, it 
will remain breezy into the holiday weekend with west winds 
gusting 25-35 mph with strongest gusts in the Laural Highlands.
